rics.meaning: API Cushing crude oil number — industry-source weekly stocks at Cushing OK.
rics.how_to_use: Released Tuesday evening before Wednesday's EIA report. Often moves prices on the prior-day Asia/Europe overnight session.

rics.meaning: API weekly crude oil imports — industry source for US crude imports, released Tuesday evening. Cross-check against EIA's official Wednesday release.
rics.how_to_use: Useful for forward-looking trade — API can drive overnight oil price moves before EIA confirms next morning. API methodology is voluntary reporting from refiners; EIA samples the full set, so discrepancies are usually resolved within 2-4 weeks of revisions.

rics.meaning: API weekly crude oil runs (refinery throughput) — same conceptual measure as aUSEIACR but industry-sourced. Total crude processed in US refineries per day.
rics.how_to_use: Drives demand for crude. Pair with utilization for tight-vs-loose signal. Hurricane season (Aug-Oct) on Gulf Coast can drop runs by 1-2mb/d for 2-3 weeks; major maintenance windows in spring and fall similarly reduce throughput.

rics.meaning: API weekly crude oil stocks (industry inventory) — total US commercial crude inventory excluding SPR. Industry-sourced; released Tuesday evenings, one day before EIA.
rics.how_to_use: Cross-check with EIA's official numbers. API often differs by 1-2 million barrels — a draw vs build divergence drives short-term oil-price moves. Markets initially trade API release; EIA next morning often confirms or reverses.

rics.meaning: API weekly distillate (diesel + heating oil) inventories — total US distillate stocks. Q4 inventory builds for winter heating; Q2 builds for trucking demand.
rics.how_to_use: More volatile than gasoline because two demand drivers: trucking (year-round, GDP-correlated) and heating (Q4-Q1, weather-correlated). Tight distillate stocks 2022-23 drove distillate crack spreads to record highs.

rics.meaning: API weekly gasoline inventories — total US gasoline stocks. Driving-season seasonality: drawdowns May-Aug as Memorial Day to Labor Day demand peaks.
rics.how_to_use: Cross-check with EIA gasoline stocks. Below 220M barrels = tight; above 245M = loose for the typical year. Inventories swing crack spreads (gasoline vs crude price differential).

rics.meaning: API weekly heating oil inventories — subset of distillate stocks (~25-30% of distillate). Q4 demand-driven for Northeast heating.
rics.how_to_use: Cross-check vs EIA heating oil stocks. Track heating-degree days (HDD) for demand pulse. Mild winters depress demand and build inventories; cold snaps drive draws and price spikes.

rics.meaning: API weekly product imports — refined product imports (gasoline, diesel, heating oil, jet fuel). Track for product-vs-crude import mix.
rics.how_to_use: US imports refined products mainly from Caribbean refineries (Trinidad, Curacao) and Europe. Falls when domestic refineries run higher; rises during US refinery outages.

rics.meaning: Test series — placeholder.
rics.how_to_use: Not for use.

rics.description: United States, EMISSIONS - CARBON DIOXIDE, Volume, Commodity Fundamentals, Annual, British Petroleum
rics.meaning: US carbon dioxide emissions, total.
rics.how_to_use: Annual EIA. Tracks US progress on emissions reductions. Has trended down post-2007.

rics.meaning: EIA crude oil imports — official measure. Halved post-shale (2007 ~10mb/d → 2024 ~6mb/d) as US production rose from ~5mb/d to ~13mb/d.
rics.how_to_use: Cross-check with API (aUSOIAIA). Track Saudi/OPEC+ vs Canadian share for geopolitical exposure: Canada is now the dominant US crude supplier (~60% of imports). Pipeline disruptions (Keystone, Enbridge) drive short-term spikes.

rics.meaning: EIA weekly petroleum products imports — official EIA measure of refined-products imports. Cross-check against API.
rics.how_to_use: Track for US refining-deficit signals: when product imports are persistently elevated, US refineries can't meet domestic demand. Used in trade-balance and consumer-fuel-price analyses.

rics.meaning: Imports, petroleum products, absolute change — week-over-week change in product imports.
rics.how_to_use: Volatility signal. Spikes during refinery outages or supply disruptions (Colonial Pipeline 2021, Hurricane Harvey 2017). Smooths to ~2-3 million bpd in normal weeks.

rics.meaning: Natural Gas Implied Flow (EIA) — backed-out demand calculated from production minus storage change. Captures total domestic + export demand for nat gas.
rics.how_to_use: Important for nat-gas storage and pricing. LNG exports have surged post-2016 (Sabine Pass, Cameron, Calcasieu Pass) — implied demand now includes ~14 Bcf/d of LNG exports. Track for cold-snap demand spikes (heating) and cooling-degree-day demand (electricity for AC).

rics.description: Production, Crude Oil Inputs into Refineries, Absolute change
rics.meaning: Crude oil inputs into refineries, absolute change (weekly) — pace of refinery throughput change.
rics.how_to_use: Captures refinery activity changes. Maintenance turnarounds (spring + fall) drop runs by 1-2 mb/d temporarily; hurricanes (Aug-Oct Gulf Coast) similar magnitude. Watch for unscheduled drops as supply-disruption signal.

rics.meaning: Distillate production, absolute change (weekly) — pace of diesel + heating oil output change.
rics.how_to_use: Track for distillate-supply tightness signals. Elevated demand + flat production = tightening market. Diesel demand correlates with trucking/freight (real-economy proxy).

rics.meaning: EIA coal production, total US.
rics.how_to_use: Long-term decline. Down >50% from 2008 peak. Replaced by gas + renewables.

rics.description: Production, EIA, Crude Oil Inputs into Refineries
rics.meaning: EIA weekly crude oil inputs into refineries — refinery throughput. Largest single use of US crude. Demand pulse for crude-oil markets.
rics.how_to_use: Tracks domestic crude demand at the refinery gate. Seasonal: peaks in summer driving season, troughs in fall maintenance turnarounds. Compare to refinery capacity utilization for slack-vs-tightness signal. Cross-check against API weekly numbers (aUSOIARA).

rics.meaning: EIA weekly distillate fuel oil production — diesel + heating oil output from US refineries. Released in EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report each Wednesday.
rics.how_to_use: Diesel demand is freight-driven (trucking + rail), a real-economy proxy. Heating oil demand is winter-weather-driven (Northeast US). Tight diesel supply in 2022 drove crack spreads to record highs — track distillate inventories alongside.

rics.meaning: EIA gasoline production.
rics.how_to_use: Gasoline output — pairs with stocks for refining-margin analysis.

rics.meaning: EIA Refinery Capacity Utilization. 85-95% normal range.
rics.how_to_use: Drops sharply during hurricane season (Gulf shut-ins) and spring/fall maintenance (turnarounds). Pair refinery inputs with crude imports + crude production for fundamental balance. Below 85% = excess capacity, weak crack spreads.

rics.meaning: Gasoline production, absolute change (weekly) — pace of gasoline output change. Tracks driving-season supply response.
rics.how_to_use: Refineries shift product slate seasonally — more gasoline in summer, more distillate in winter. Watch for unusual divergences from seasonal pattern.

rics.description: Production, Refinery Capacity Utilization, Absolute change
rics.meaning: Refinery capacity utilization, weekly absolute change — pace of refinery slack tightening or loosening. EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report.
rics.how_to_use: Refinery utilization ~85-95% in normal operation. Hurricanes (Gulf Coast) and maintenance turnarounds drive temporary drops. Sustained sub-85% suggests demand softness or capacity loss; sustained 95%+ flags capacity constraint and crack-spread expansion.

rics.description: Stock Levels, Cushing, Oklahoma Crude Oil excluding SPR, Absolute change
rics.meaning: Cushing OK crude oil stocks ex-SPR, absolute change WoW.
rics.how_to_use: WTI futures-deliverable supply. Below 25M bbl = tank tops empty risk.

rics.description: Stock Levels, Distillate over 500 ppm sulfur, Absolute change
rics.meaning: Stock levels, distillate over 500ppm sulfur, absolute change — high-sulfur distillate inventory pace of change.
rics.how_to_use: Smaller specialty market. Track for bunker fuel and non-road diesel supply dynamics. Mainstream ULSD inventory (aUSOILDA) is the meaningful market gauge.

rics.description: Stock Levels, EIA Weekly Crude Imports
rics.meaning: EIA weekly crude oil imports stock levels — companion to import flow (aUSEIACI). Tracks aggregate US-bound crude inventory.
rics.how_to_use: Use the flow series (aUSEIACI) for high-frequency tracking. Levels reflect logistics pipeline (in-transit cargoes plus port stocks).

rics.description: Stock Levels, EIA, Cushing, Oklahoma Crude Oil excluding SPR
rics.meaning: Cushing OK crude oil stocks ex-SPR — WTI futures delivery point. The most-watched single inventory location.
rics.how_to_use: Below 25M bbl = tank tops empty risk; above 80M = oversupply. WTI-Brent spread widens (WTI discount) when Cushing is full; narrows when low.

rics.description: Stock Levels, EIA, Distillate over 500 ppm sulfur
rics.meaning: EIA weekly distillate stocks (>500ppm sulfur) — non-ULSD high-sulfur distillate. Used in non-road/marine fuel and some heating applications.
rics.how_to_use: Smaller pool than ULSD (the dominant US diesel grade). Track for non-road fuel market dynamics. Mostly relevant to specialty-fuel markets and bunker-fuel applications.

rics.meaning: Total US Gasoline Stocks. Released weekly with EIA petroleum status report.
rics.how_to_use: Builds during winter (low driving demand), draws during summer (peak driving). Below 5-year range = bullish gasoline cracks. Pre-Memorial Day stock builds often signal weak demand or oversupply.

rics.meaning: EIA distillate stocks, PADD 1 (East Coast) — distillate inventories in PADD 1 (Northeast US). Heating-oil-heavy due to NE residential heating demand.
rics.how_to_use: Most weather-sensitive PADD for distillate. Cold winter draws drive product imports from Europe. PADD 1 supply matters for Northeast heating-oil prices and fuel-oil markets.

rics.meaning: EIA distillate stocks, PADD 1A (New England) — sub-region of PADD 1. Highest heating-oil exposure (Maine through Connecticut).
rics.how_to_use: Most weather-driven inventory in US. Mild winters → builds; cold snaps → severe draws. Heating-oil dealer inventory turnover is key real-time indicator.

rics.meaning: EIA distillate stocks, PADD 1B (Mid-Atlantic) — NY, NJ, PA, DE, MD region. Mix of heating and trucking demand.
rics.how_to_use: More commercial/trucking-driven than PADD 1A. Pipeline-supplied (Colonial Pipeline). Watch for major pipeline disruptions impacting Mid-Atlantic supply.

rics.meaning: EIA distillate stocks, PADD 1C (Lower Atlantic) — VA through FL. Less heating exposure than upper PADD 1; more trucking/agricultural demand.
rics.how_to_use: Pipeline + local refinery supplied. Hurricane-season disruptions (Aug-Oct) can sharply tighten regional supply.

rics.meaning: EIA distillate stocks, PADD 2 (Midwest) — Midwest US distillate inventory. Trucking/agriculture-heavy demand profile.
rics.how_to_use: Pipeline-supplied from Gulf Coast. Watch for tightness during ag-harvest periods (Sep-Nov) when farm diesel demand surges.

rics.meaning: PADD 3 (Gulf Coast) distillate stocks.
rics.how_to_use: Largest refining region. Gulf Coast crack spreads pricing reference.

rics.meaning: EIA distillate stocks, PADD 4 (Rocky Mountains) — small-volume PADD with limited refining capacity. Mostly truck/rail-supplied.
rics.how_to_use: Smallest PADD by distillate inventory. Local supply tightness can drive regional price spikes (Western Slope CO, MT, WY). Less liquid market than coastal PADDs.

rics.meaning: EIA distillate stocks, PADD 5 (West Coast) — West Coast US distillate inventory. CARB-spec fuel requirements complicate cross-PADD product transfers.
rics.how_to_use: Insulated from other PADDs by quality requirements. CARB diesel standards mean West Coast inventory is functionally separate market. Watch for CA-specific supply/demand events.

rics.meaning: Reformulated gasoline stocks.
rics.how_to_use: RBOB grade — summer-spec gasoline. Tightens approaching summer driving.

rics.description: Stock Levels, EIA, Strategic Petroleum Reserve
rics.meaning: Strategic Petroleum Reserve stocks. Drained ~200M bbl in 2022 (Russia/Ukraine response under Biden admin). Refilling has been slow.
rics.how_to_use: Below 350M bbl is historically low. Refill pace (target $67-72/bbl) tested by oil price moves. SPR can release ~1M bbl/day for sustained periods.

rics.description: Stock Levels, EIA, Total Crude Oil excluding SPR
rics.meaning: Total US Crude Oil Stocks excluding SPR — EIA weekly Wednesday release. The single most market-watched US oil-inventory series.
rics.how_to_use: Big surprises vs API/consensus drive WTI intraday by 2-5%. Cushing-specific stocks (aUSSCCO) matter most for WTI futures (delivery point). Below 25M bbl Cushing = tank-tops empty risk; above 80M = oversupply pressure.

rics.meaning: Total US Distillate Stocks (diesel + heating oil). Industrial + freight + winter heating demand.
rics.how_to_use: Winter heating-oil cushion gauge — heavily watched in Q4. Distillate cracks often diverge from gasoline cracks based on freight cycle (diesel) vs travel cycle (gasoline).

rics.meaning: Gasoline stock levels, absolute change (weekly) — pace of gasoline-inventory change.
rics.how_to_use: Negative readings (draws) common in summer driving season; positive (builds) in winter. Below seasonal norm = tight market = price-supportive. Pair with refining margins for crack-spread direction.

rics.description: Stock Levels, Natural Gas in Underground Storage, Lower 48 States, Absolute change
rics.meaning: Natural gas in underground storage, Lower 48, absolute change.
rics.how_to_use: Weekly NG storage change. Inverse of demand minus production.

rics.description: Stock Levels, Reformulated Gasoline, Absolute change
rics.meaning: Reformulated gasoline (RFG) stock levels, absolute change — RFG is used in major metro areas (CA, NY, NJ, etc.) for clean-air requirements.
rics.how_to_use: Smaller stock pool than conventional gasoline. Track for regional supply tightness in metro markets. Subject to specific summer-blend mandates (RVP rules) that drive seasonal shifts.

rics.description: Stock Levels, Total Crude Oil excluding SPR, Absolute change
rics.meaning: Total Crude Oil stock levels (excluding SPR), absolute change — week-over-week change in commercial crude inventory.
rics.how_to_use: Build vs draw is the key oil-price-driving signal. Builds = bearish (oversupply); draws = bullish (tightness). Winter: typically builds; spring: typically draws. Seasonality matters.

rics.description: Stock Levels, Total Distillate, Absolute change
rics.meaning: Total Distillate stock levels, absolute change — week-over-week change in diesel + heating oil inventory.
rics.how_to_use: Build/draw signal for distillate market. Trucking-demand-driven year-round + heating-demand seasonal Q4. Watch for tight readings as diesel-crack-spread expansion signal.

rics.description: Weekly U.S. Ending Stocks of Fuel Ethanol, Commodity Fundamentals, Weekly, EIA - Energy Information Administration, United States
rics.meaning: US ending stocks of fuel ethanol — weekly.
rics.how_to_use: Ethanol blendstock. Tied to gasoline demand and corn prices.

rics.description: Weekly U.S. Oxygenate Plant Production of Fuel Ethanol, Commodity Fundamentals, Weekly, EIA - Energy Information Administration, United States
rics.meaning: Weekly US oxygenate plant production of fuel ethanol — domestic ethanol production for gasoline blending (E10, E15, E85).
rics.how_to_use: RFS (Renewable Fuel Standard) mandates drive ~13B gallons/year. Corn-price-sensitive on input side. Track for ag-policy implications: corn demand for ethanol affects food prices.

rics.meaning: Soybean oil export sales, net.
rics.how_to_use: Weekly USDA Export Sales report. Drives soyoil futures.
